<a id="guarantees"></a>

## What the gate guarantees

This is the spec the gate is reviewed against (`scripts/checks/architecture-spec.mjs`). A finding is a **failing test** against one of these clauses; a shape a clause puts outside is not one, and widening a clause is the owner's call. Each clause names the self-tests that prove it, and the self-test fails when one of them is missing. Under every clause the threat model is an honest agent's eager mistake: an agent that sets out to forge (dropping its attribution line, rewriting the CI step) is not stopped by any check, and review is the backstop for that.

**S1. Money calls are found.** In A1's scope, every member call `.transfers.create(`, `.transfers.createReversal(`, `.refunds.create(` or `.payouts.create(` is found, an optional call (`create?.(`) included: inside a template's interpolation, in a callback, split across lines, after a nested template or a regex (one that starts a line or follows a brace-less `if (…)` head too). Text in a comment, a string or a template's own text is never a call. Comments and strings are read by ONE scanner, so they can't disagree about where a template ends.

- **Outside:** a call through a stored reference (`const t = stripe.transfers; t.create(`) or a computed member (`stripe["transfers"]`); code biome would not accept.
- **Proved by:** "A1 ignores the owner modules, tests and comments", "A1 sees optional chaining and a call split across lines", "A1 sees a money call inside an interpolation, after a nested template, and after a regex holding a quote", "A1 keys: a multi-line string above the call keeps its function, and a string never matches", "a URL in a nested template, a comment-like template or a regex at the start of a line hides no call", "A1 sees an optional call and a regex after a brace-less if".

**S2. A key names where its violation sits.** A line-level violation's key names the function, method (a `#private` one too), class field, route or callback it sits in, read from biome's indentation, and from the violation's own line for a one-line arrow (`const pay = (p) => …`), so a fix in one named place can't pay for a new violation in another. A parenthesised value (`const paid = (await x()).map(`) and a call to a name starting `function` are no declarations. Routes are read in a worker's source only, from a registration on one name (`app.post(`) or chained (`.post(`). A misread name can only merge two keys; it never hides a violation.

- **Outside:** two functions with the same name in one file; code biome has not formatted; in a worker's source, a call shaped like a route registration on one name (`api.post('/x', …)`), which is read as a route.
- **Proved by:** "a call key names its function, so a fix in one cannot pay for a call in another", "the enclosing name survives a multi-line signature and destructured parameters", "routes in the form biome writes get their own keys; a header read or a cache get names nothing", "a method head needs its body: a call or an arrow callback is no method", "a wrapped or arrow return type still names its method, and a chained, assigned or constant route names itself", "a key names a one-line arrow, a #private method, a parenthesised value and functionsOf(); routes are read only in a worker".

**S3. Every rate limit a route uses is read.** In a worker's route files, every use of `procedure`, `multipartProcedure`, `binaryUploadProcedure` or `rateLimit` (bare, or through an `import * as` namespace of `@codex/worker-utils` or `@codex/security`) is a direct call whose options the gate reads, an object key (judged by the code before it, however far back), or an entry of an import list. Any other use fails as unreadable, and so does a dynamic `import(…)` or `require(…)` whose argument is not a quoted literal naming another module (a limiter module, a template with a substitution, a variable). A preset with no binding in every environment of the worker's wrangler.jsonc fails.

- **Outside:** a limiter reached through another module of this repo that re-exports it.
- **Proved by:** "RATE-LIMIT-BINDING: the default preset, every env, every limiter, and what it cannot read", "RATE-LIMIT-BINDING fails what it cannot read, and follows what it can", "RATE-LIMIT-BINDING: every alias form fails; reading a property passes", "RATE-LIMIT-BINDING: any use but a call, a key or an import entry fails", "RATE-LIMIT-BINDING: a key is judged by the code before it, and a computed or template import is unreadable".

**S4. A CLAUDE.md pays for what it imports.** DOC-BUDGET counts the words of every import a CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md makes, read with Claude Code's own grammar (2.1.330: an `@` at the start of a text run or after whitespace, then every non-space character, cut at `#`; code blocks, code spans and HTML comments skipped; emphasis and a link's label read), that resolves to a tracked file relative to the importing file (any number of `./` and `../`, into a dot-folder, with or without an extension), up to 5 hops, each file once. A path keeps its punctuation, as Claude Code keeps it: `@README.` names `README.`.

- **Outside:** at commit time, an edit to the imported file alone: CI judges the importer; an import of a file outside the repository (`@~/…`, `@/…`); an import Claude Code skips that this still counts (in a table, an HTML block or an indented code block): the budget's safe side.
- **Proved by:** "DOC-BUDGET counts the words a CLAUDE.md imports", "DOC-BUDGET follows an import up two folders, into a dot-folder or without an extension, to 5 hops", "DOC-BUDGET reads imports as Claude Code does: route characters, emphasis, a full stop and a parenthesis".

**S5. Debt only shrinks.** A violation whose key isn't pinned, or a size above its pin, fails. A fix fails the commit that touches its file until it is banked, and the pull request that made it. `--lower` only lowers or removes. In a pull request a file may grow no further than the base measured unless the owner signed its pin: growing into a pin above what the base measured needs the same countersign as raising it. That sign covers the pin's stale headroom, and every run lists what it covers.

- **Outside:** a release PR or a push to dev or main: there, unbanked fixes and growth into a stale pin are notices.
- **Proved by:** "one more of a pinned key fails as more", "a fix cannot pay for a new violation in the same file", "--lower only lowers or removes; it never raises or adds", "--ci in a PR: a fix this change made blocks wherever it is; one dev left behind is a notice", "--ci in a PR: headroom a fix left unbanked on dev cannot be spent", "growing into a stale pin is signed like a raise, and a release PR only notes it", "the base copy judges growth into a stale pin, and a trunk push notes it".

**S6. What loosens the gate is a closed list.** These, and only these, are loosening items: (1) a raised or added baseline pin, or growth into one (S5); (2) a new, copied, moved or renewed exception; (3) the gate's own code: every tracked file in `scripts/checks/` but the baseline, `.github/workflows/static_analysis.yml`, `.husky/pre-commit`, gate.sh, and a calling workflow's triggers, concurrency or static-analysis job; (4) what another gate runs: a file a gate command runs with node, tsx, ts-node or vite-node (also behind `VAR=value`, `env`, `cross-env`, `dotenv … --`, `time`, `nice` or `exec`, or as a `./file.mjs`), with what it imports and preloads (`--import ./x.mjs`) and its tracked `--env-file`; every pnpm script a gate command reaches, with its `pre`/`post` scripts (a bare `pnpm <name>` with no such script runs <name> as a command, as `pnpm exec` does); every task in a gate's turbo task's `dependsOn` closure, read from the root and every package `turbo.json`, at each package's `turbo.json` and as each package's script (added, changed or deleted); every workspace package's install lifecycle scripts; the root `turbo.json`; `pnpm-workspace.yaml`'s `packages:` list (in any YAML form) and its `scriptShell`, `shellEmulator`, `ignoreScripts` and `enablePrePostScripts`; `.npmrc`; `.pnpmfile.cjs`; a gate's declared `files`; and a rise in a gate's `ratchets`; (5) Biome's reach: any `biome.json`, `biome.jsonc`, `.biome.json` or `.biome.jsonc` and the local files each `extends`, and any `.gitignore` or `.ignore`, at any depth, compared at its own path (a move is a new file there), unless the change only deletes plain lines or adds `!` lines. A gate command the gate can't resolve to tracked files and scripts (a first word that is no listed leaf binary, a `NODE_OPTIONS` preload, a pnpm built-in), and a manifest it derives parts from but can't parse, are registry errors, never a pass.

- **Outside:** tool versions: a devDependency or lockfile bump, a patch under `patches/`, a key of pnpm-workspace.yaml but the five above; a package's own tsconfig, a tool's own config (`vite.config.*`), and any other file a tool reads that this list doesn't name; a package preset a Biome config extends, a symlink's target, and an env file a wrapper loads (`dotenv -e`); the allowlists inside the other gates' own scripts: they are gate files, so every edit to one asks, a shrink included; CI environment variables and runner images.
- **Proved by:** "a raised pin needs a G0-RAISE trailer in a commit, with a real reason", "a new exception and a change to the gate itself need one too", "a pnpm script a gate runs is part of the gate", "any file in the gate folder is gate code, and a gate part that is no file is a registry error", "what a gate runs is derived from its commands, followed as a shell would, plus what it declares", "a calling workflow is part of the gate only where the gate depends on it", "a nested biome config, a new .gitignore line or a package turbo.json is part of the gate", "an ignore file loosens by a new rule, a lost negation, a new order or a move; a .ignore and a .biome.json count", "a deleted turbo-task script, a pre/post or lifecycle script, the root turbo.json and .npmrc are gate parts", "a gate command the reader cannot resolve is a registry error; the forms it can are followed", "the command reader follows tsx, wrappers, preloads and pnpm's exec fallback; anything else is a registry error", "pnpm-workspace.yaml is read in every YAML form, and a manifest the gate cannot parse is a registry error", "every task typecheck reaches counts in every package; the workspace script settings and a Biome config's local extends are gate parts".

**S7. A countersign covers exactly what the owner signed.** A `G0-RAISE: KEY@hash — reason` trailer counts only in a commit in base..HEAD with no `Co-Authored-By: Claude` line, and a reason of three words or more with no `<placeholder>`. It covers its item only at that hash. A hash is taken over a canonical form (a pin's keys sorted, JSON keys sorted, a whole JSON file parsed), so re-sorting signs nothing away; any other change to the item, a tightening included, asks again. Every exception the change adds, copies, moves or renews is listed under its hash.

- **Outside:** a forged trailer in a commit without its attribution line.
- **Proved by:** "the gate's own pasted output, or an agent's trailer, is not a countersign", "a countersign covers what it signed: loosening the same item after it needs a new one", "a hash binds the countersign: an amend, or a cherry-pick onto another change, is asked again", "a countersign needs a three-word reason, and covers only its own entry", "a pin hashes in canonical order, a path with a space can be signed, and every exception a hash covers is listed".

**S8. The pull request into dev judges; the base copy judges with it.** A pull request into dev fails on anything unsigned. A push to dev or main, and a release PR from this repository's dev into main, only note it. When a change edits the gate folder (`scripts/checks/` and the runner's entry folders, not just the baseline), the base commit's copy of the gate also judges the countersigns and the growth into stale pins, finding the base itself, and lists what its own rules find. A base that holds the gate's baseline or rules page with no runner at any listed entry path fails the run (exit 2). The owner's sign past a base copy that can't run covers only that base copy's code and the gate code it was signed for, the calling workflows' gate parts included.

- **Outside:** the `edited` pull_request event (a base switched after CI ran); a change to only static_analysis.yml, .husky/pre-commit, gate.sh or a caller job: it runs no base copy, whose code would be the change's own; a merge queue: no caller triggers on merge_group, and WP-6 makes the static-analysis job itself the required check.
- **Proved by:** "a push to dev, or a release PR, only notes an unsigned loosening", "when a change edits the gate, the base's copy of the gate judges it too", "a PR whose base is HEAD itself is an error, not a pass", "a base copy that can't run is an error the owner can sign past", "ciBase knows its events and stops on any other", "ciBase: a pull request from dev is a release", "a base that holds the gate where no entry path looks is an error; a baseline-only change runs no base copy", "the sign past a base copy covers the calling workflows and survives a dev move".

**S9. Exit codes.** 0: everything passed. 1: a violation, or an unsigned loosening. 2: the gate can't run: a registry error, a git error, a gate command it can't read, a base it can't find. A crash is never 0 or 1.

- **Proved by:** "a gate that cannot run exits 2, never 0 or 1", "a broken gate module exits 2, not 1", "a malformed rule is an error, never a silently skipped rule".

## Adding a rule

Pick the strongest **mechanism** first, then the strongest **channel** that can run it:

1. **Architecture:** one owner and one way, so the wrong import cannot build.
2. **Types:** an illegal state that does not compile.
3. **A rule on this page:** its message names the one fix.
4. **A test:** a fixture taken from a real past mistake.
5. **Docs:** judgment calls only; nothing fails when an agent skips them.

A rule here is one entry in `scripts/checks/architecture-rules.mjs`. The self-test fails unless the rule has a fixture that fires and names the past mistake it reproduces.

## The baseline

A rule that measures a file (SIZE, DOC-BUDGET) pins its size. Every other rule pins the **key** of each violation it allows: the call and the function it sits in (`transferPendingGroup>transfers.create(`), the dead link's target, the missing path. So a fix can't pay for a new violation in the same file: the new one's key isn't pinned, and it fails even when the count is unchanged.

- A violation whose key isn't pinned, or a size above its pin, is new, and fails.
- A fixed violation, a smaller size or a file that is gone must be **banked** with `pnpm check:arch --lower`, so the headroom it freed can't be spent later. It fails the commit that touches the file (bank it with `--lower --staged`, which banks what the index holds and stages the baseline), and the pull request that made the fix: the violation still existed at the base, in whatever file. A fix already left unbanked on `dev` is only a notice, so two PRs can't merge into a red branch, and a release PR from `dev` isn't blocked by them.
- In a pull request a pin allows no more than the base still had. A fix left unbanked on `dev` is headroom no later change spends quietly: growing into it fails unless the owner countersigns that pin, with the same line a raise of it takes. A release PR only notes it.
- A renamed file carries its pin to the new path; `--lower` moves it (renames are found against `origin/dev`).
- `--lower` only ever lowers or removes. `--init --rule <ID>` seeds the block for a rule added later.
- RULES-DOC and CI-GATES can't be held in the baseline at all: their drift is fixed, never pinned.

<a id="raises"></a>

## Loosening the gate

Anything that loosens the gate needs the **owner's** countersign: a trailer line in a commit message in the change. It counts only in a commit with no `Co-Authored-By: Claude` line, so the agent that loosened the gate can't sign for it; it asks the owner, and the failure prints the one-liner to run. Each line names the item with `@` and a short hash of its content as the change leaves it, so a countersign covers exactly what the owner saw: an amend, a cherry-pick, or a change to the same item merged in from the base changes the hash, and the gate asks again with the new one. The countersign lives in the commit, not the PR description, so `git blame` keeps it next to what it explains.

A pull request into `dev` is where this is judged. A push to `dev` or `main`, and a release PR from `dev`, only note anything unsigned: two PRs that each signed the same file produce a merged state neither signed.

| What loosens | Trailer |
|---|---|
| A raised or added baseline pin | `G0-RAISE: <RULE> <file>@<hash> — <reason>` |
| Every pin of a rule the base doesn't have yet | `G0-RAISE: <RULE> *@<hash> — <reason>` |
| A new, copied, moved or renewed exception (below) | `G0-RAISE: <RULE> <file>@<hash> — <reason>` |
| A change to the gate itself: any file in `scripts/checks/` but the baseline, its CI steps, the hook, gate.sh | `G0-RAISE: GATE <path>@<hash> — <reason>` |
| A change to what another gate runs: a file its command runs (and what that file imports); a pnpm script it reaches, with its pre/post scripts; a turbo task's script in any package, added, changed or deleted; any package's install lifecycle scripts; the root `turbo.json`; a package's `turbo.json` at the tasks the gate's task depends on; `pnpm-workspace.yaml`'s `packages:`; `.npmrc`; a gate's config (`files`) | `G0-RAISE: GATE <path>@<hash>`, `GATE <file>#scripts.<name>@<hash>`, `GATE <pkg>/turbo.json#tasks.<name>@<hash>` |
| A config a gate finds by pattern (`filesMatching`): any biome config, or an ignore file (`.gitignore`, `.ignore`) that gains a plain line, loses a negation, changes order or moves (Biome skips what it matches) | `G0-RAISE: GATE <path>@<hash> — <reason>` |
| A rise in another gate's own baseline (`ratchets`) | `G0-RAISE: GATE <path>@<hash> — <reason>` |
| A change to the triggers, concurrency or static-analysis job of a calling workflow | `G0-RAISE: GATE <workflow>@<hash> — <reason>` |

A reason is at least three words, with no `<placeholder>` left in it. `pnpm check:arch --ci` runs the check against the change's base, and `--raises <ref>` runs it alone. When the change edits the gate's own code, the **base commit's** copy of the gate judges the countersigns as well, finding the base itself, so a bug in the new copy can't approve itself. It also runs its rules over the change and lists anything it finds, next to the GATE countersign, so the owner sees what the new gate stops catching before signing. If the base's copy can't run at all (an import or flag it can't follow), the owner can sign past it for the gate code as it stands: the gate prints `G0-RAISE: GATE base-judge@<hash> — <reason>`, and any later edit to the gate asks again.

That list is closed ([S6](#guarantees)): a gate command the gate can't resolve to tracked files and scripts is a registry error, never a pass. What this holds against is an honest agent's eager mistake: signing its own raise, or breaking the gate while refactoring it. An agent that sets out to forge (dropping its attribution line, rewriting the CI step that runs the gate) is not stopped by any check here; review is the backstop for that.

<a id="exceptions"></a>

## Exceptions

One violation of a line-level rule can be excepted by a comment on the line above it. The exception names one rule, an expiry date, the person who granted it and a reason, and it needs the owner's countersign (above):

```ts
// arch-ignore A1 until=2026-12-31 by=<owner> — <reason>
```

In markdown, use an HTML comment. One exception excuses one violation, the one on the next line: the countersign covers the exception together with that line, so copying it, or moving it onto another violation, needs a new one. The date may be at most 90 days out: an exception is temporary by definition. The gate fails an exception that has expired, runs too long, excuses nothing, is malformed, names a rule that doesn't apply to the file, or names a rule that measures a whole file (SIZE, DOC-BUDGET, whose exception is its baseline pin) or can't be excepted (LAYERS, DOC-INDEX, RULES-DOC, CI-GATES).

## Rules

### A1

**Money moves only through the payments ledger.**

Transfers, reversals, refunds and payouts move real money. When each module calls Stripe itself, the ledger, the clawback rules and the payout thresholds can be bypassed by whichever caller forgets them. The owners are the four @codex/payments modules that record every movement. Each call is pinned by the function it sits in (`transferPendingGroup>transfers.create(`), so a new call in another function fails even where an old one was fixed. Known limit: a text pattern can't follow an alias (`const t = stripe.transfers; t.create(`); the owner refactor and the types epic (Codex-omrp2) close that.

- **Applies to:** `packages/*/src/**/*.{ts,mts,cts,js,mjs,cjs}`, `workers/*/src/**/*.{ts,mts,cts,js,mjs,cjs}`, `apps/*/src/**/*.{ts,mts,cts,js,mjs,cjs}`, `scripts/**/*.{ts,mts,cts,js,mjs,cjs}`, `{packages,workers,apps}/*/scripts/**/*.{ts,mts,cts,js,mjs,cjs}`
- **Except:** `**/*.test.ts`, `**/*.spec.ts`, `**/*.type-check.ts`, `**/*.d.ts`, `**/__tests__/**`, `**/__mocks__/**`, `scripts/checks/**`, `packages/payments/src/payout-ledger.ts`, `packages/payments/src/clawback.ts`, `packages/payments/src/refund.ts`, `packages/payments/src/bank-payouts.ts`
- **Checked by:** `call`, matching `\b(?:transfers\s*\??\.\s*(?:create|createReversal)|refunds\s*\??\.\s*create|payouts\s*\??\.\s*create)\s*(?:\?\.\s*)?\(`
- **Fix:** Move the money through @codex/payments (payout-ledger, clawback, refund or bank-payouts); never call these Stripe APIs directly.

### LAYERS

**A package depends only on lower layers.**

Upward and sideways dependencies are how a payments package ends up importing purchase, and how a 9,000-line service becomes impossible to split. The layer map is today's graph, so the rule starts green and any new edge is a visible decision.

- **Applies to:** `packages/*/package.json`, `workers/*/package.json`, `apps/*/package.json`
- **Checked by:** `package-graph`
- **Fix:** Move the shared code down a layer, or add the edge to SAME_LAYER_EDGES in scripts/checks/architecture-rules.mjs with its reason.

### SIZE

**A money file never grows; a new one stays under 800 lines.**

The money services grew to 9,015 and 5,643 lines one urgent fix at a time. Pinning every large file at its size makes each change extract a module instead.

- **Applies to:** `packages/payments/src/**/*.ts`, `packages/purchase/src/**/*.ts`, `packages/subscription/src/**/*.ts`, `packages/agreements/src/**/*.ts`, `workers/ecom-api/src/**/*.ts`
- **Except:** `**/*.test.ts`, `**/*.spec.ts`, `**/*.type-check.ts`, `**/*.d.ts`, `**/__tests__/**`, `**/__mocks__/**`
- **Checked by:** `line-count`, a new or unpinned file may have up to 800 lines, (measures lines; the baseline pins larger files at their size)
- **Fix:** Extract the change into a new domain module instead of growing this file.

### DOC-LINK

**Every relative markdown link resolves.**

The 2026-11-15 docs census found 34 dead links outside the archive. A dead link sends an agent to a file that was moved, renamed or never written, and it then guesses.

- **Applies to:** `**/*.md`
- **Except:** `docs/archive/**`
- **Checked by:** `md-link`
- **Fix:** Point the link at the file as it is now, or remove it.

### DOC-PATH

**Every repo path a doc cites exists.**

One cited repo path in six was dead (352 outside the archive). A doc that names a file that is gone teaches an agent a codebase that no longer exists. Placeholders like [domain], <name> and globs are exempt.

- **Applies to:** `**/*.md`
- **Except:** `docs/archive/**`
- **Checked by:** `md-path`
- **Fix:** Update the path to where the code lives now, or drop the citation.

### DOC-INDEX

**Every doc under docs/ is listed in docs/README.md.**

85 of 147 docs were cited nowhere in the repo. A doc nobody can find is never updated, and it keeps answering searches with stale content.

- **Applies to:** `docs/**/*.md`
- **Except:** `docs/README.md`, `docs/archive/**`, `docs/handover/**`
- **Checked by:** `doc-index`
- **Fix:** Link the doc (or its folder) from the right section of docs/README.md.

### DOC-SESSION

**No tracked file cites the gitignored session notes.**

docs/handover is gitignored, so CI and every other machine see a dead reference. Durable knowledge belongs in a tracked doc.

- **Applies to:** `**/*.{md,ts,js,mjs,cjs,json,jsonc,yml,yaml,svelte,sh,py,toml}`
- **Except:** `docs/archive/**`, `docs/handover/**`, `docs/architecture/rules.md`, `scripts/checks/architecture-baseline.json`
- **Checked by:** `cite`
- **Fix:** Move what the reference needs into a tracked doc and cite that instead.

### DOC-BUDGET

**A CLAUDE.md never grows past its word budget.**

36 of 38 CLAUDE.md files were over budget (the root had 3,616 words against 1,500). Every word is loaded into every agent session in that folder, so length is paid on every task.

- **Applies to:** `**/CLAUDE.md`, `**/AGENTS.md`
- **Not matched yet:** `**/AGENTS.md`
- **Checked by:** `word-count`, budget `CLAUDE.md` 1,500, every other 600 words, (measures words; the baseline pins larger files at their size)
- **Fix:** Move reference material into docs/ and link it; keep the CLAUDE.md to the rules an agent needs in this folder.

### RATE-LIMIT-BINDING

**Every rate-limit preset a worker's routes use has its binding in every environment.**

A preset with no wrangler binding fails OPEN: every request passes and rate_limit.fail_open is logged on each one. wrangler does not inherit ratelimits or Durable Object bindings into env.* blocks, so each environment needs its own. The preset-to-binding map is read from limits.ts, not copied.

- **Applies to:** `workers/*/src/**/*.ts`, `workers/*/wrangler.jsonc`, `packages/constants/src/limits.ts`
- **Except:** `**/*.test.ts`, `**/*.spec.ts`, `**/*.type-check.ts`, `**/*.d.ts`, `**/__tests__/**`, `**/__mocks__/**`
- **Checked by:** `lists-agree`
- **Fix:** Add the binding to that worker's wrangler.jsonc, in every env block, in the same change (see the namespace_id scheme in its comment).

### RULES-DOC

**The rules page equals the registry.**

A rules page written by hand drifts: the payments architecture doc said a money file was 5,097 lines long when it was 9,015. This page is rendered from the registry, so a rule can't exist only in prose, and the prose can't describe a rule that doesn't run.

- **Applies to:** `docs/architecture/rules.md`, `scripts/checks/architecture-*.mjs`
- **Checked by:** `generated`
- **Fix:** Run pnpm check:arch --write-rules and commit the page with the registry change.

### CI-GATES

**The registry's gate list and the static-analysis job's steps agree.**

gate.sh, the local copy of CI, skipped five of CI's static gates, and PR #705 went red in CI minutes after passing it (Codex-kxdz9). With the list held here and checked both ways, a gate added to CI is run locally too, and a gate dropped from CI can't stay listed. A step switched off by if: or continue-on-error counts as dropped, the calling workflows must run the job unconditionally, and every pnpm script a gate runs must exist, because pnpm --filter exits 0 for a missing one.

- **Applies to:** `.github/workflows/static_analysis.yml`, `.github/workflows/testing.yml`, `.github/workflows/main-gate.yml`, `scripts/checks/architecture-rules.mjs`, `package.json`, `{apps,packages,workers}/*/package.json`
- **Checked by:** `lists-agree`
- **Fix:** Add the step to GATES (or CI_SETUP_STEPS) in scripts/checks/architecture-rules.mjs, or add the missing step to the workflow.

## Other CI gates

The static-analysis job runs these too. The CI-GATES rule keeps this list and the job's steps equal in both directions, and `pnpm check:arch --gates` runs each one locally (`gate.sh` calls it).

| Gate | Checks | Runs |
|---|---|---|
| BIOME | Biome lint and format; every diagnostic fails | `pnpm check:ci`<br>reads `biome.json`<br>reads any `**/biome.json`<br>reads any `**/biome.jsonc`<br>reads any `**/.biome.json`<br>reads any `**/.biome.jsonc`<br>reads any `**/.gitignore`<br>reads any `**/.ignore` |
| TYPECHECK | TypeScript across the monorepo | `pnpm typecheck`<br>reads `tsconfig.json`<br>reads `tsconfig.build.json`<br>reads `config/tsconfig.json`<br>reads `config/tsconfig/base.json`<br>reads `config/tsconfig/package.json`<br>reads `config/tsconfig/package-typecheck.json`<br>reads `config/tsconfig/worker.json`<br>reads `apps/web/svelte.config.js` |
| SETUP-ORDER | Every workflow sets up pnpm before setup-node | `node --test scripts/checks/check-workflow-setup-order.test.mjs`<br>`node scripts/checks/check-workflow-setup-order.mjs` |
| BRAND-BOUNDARY | The public bundle never imports the brand editor | `pnpm --filter web run check:brand-boundary:test`<br>`pnpm --filter web run check:brand-boundary` |
| DIALOG-STRUCTURE | Dialogs are built from the shared Dialog parts | `pnpm --filter web run check:dialog-structure:test`<br>`pnpm --filter web run check:dialog-structure` |
| LOAD-RETRY | A load failure renders the shared LoadFailedAlert with Retry | `pnpm --filter web run check:load-retry:test`<br>`pnpm --filter web run check:load-retry` |
| DATA-ACCESS | Cache-Control from presets, no floating KV write, shared search inputs, deterministic sql time, VersionedCache gets waitUntil | `node --test scripts/checks/check-data-access-contract.test.mjs`<br>`node scripts/checks/check-data-access-contract.mjs` |
| SVELTE-BASELINE | svelte-check finds no error beyond its baseline | `pnpm --filter web exec paraglide-js compile --project ./project.inlang --outdir ./src/paraglide`<br>`pnpm --filter web run check:svelte-baseline:test`<br>`pnpm --filter web run check:svelte-baseline`<br>reads `apps/web/svelte.config.js`<br>its baseline `apps/web/scripts/svelte-check-baseline.json` |
| ARCH | The rules on this page, and countersigned loosening | `node --test scripts/checks/check-architecture.test.mjs`<br>`node scripts/checks/check-architecture.mjs --ci` |
